name: YNX Mail

seo.title: YNX Mail — Signed communication for YNX identities
seo.metaDescription: YNX Mail provides signed @handle communication with drafts, threads, attachments, recovery controls and an optional provider bridge whose delivery states remain explicitly separated.

publicStatus.statusLabel: Testnet source verified locally; not publicly deployed

features: Signed @handle native delivery with threads, replies, drafts, search, archive, spam and block controls
Bounded attachments and selected-context AI draft workflows requiring review
Provider-neutral Internet Mail Bridge with truthful queued, accepted, delivered, bounced, complained and failed states
Persistent webhook replay protection, recipient-hash suppression and bounded dead-letter recovery
Mode-restricted backup and verified restore of Mail state and sender identity
riskAndStatus: Internet provider delivery is not publicly enabled and no verified sender domain or DNS evidence exists.
Provider acceptance does not mean delivered or read; open and click telemetry never establishes YNX user-read state.
Current Android, iOS and desktop artifacts are not rebuilt, installed or hosted for this source commit.
The self-contained backup contains sensitive key material and requires an approved encrypted operator boundary.
Message bodies and attachments are not end-to-end encrypted.
Central Wallet, Cloud malware scanning, Trust operations, Monitor alerts and Data Fabric event acceptance remain incomplete.

assets.note: No current-source public logo, icon, screenshot or download artifact is claimed by this package.

faq.question: Is YNX Mail publicly available?
faq.answer: No. The current source is tested locally, but no public runtime, current-source download or store release is verified.

faq.question: Does provider acceptance mean the recipient received or read the message?
faq.answer: No. Provider acceptance, receiving-server delivery and YNX user-read are separate facts. YNX Mail does not infer user-read from provider open or click telemetry.

faq.question: Can YNX Mail send Internet email?
faq.answer: A provider adapter and signed webhook flow are implemented locally. Internet delivery remains disabled until a provider account, verified sender domain, DNS records, public webhook and abuse operations are verified.

faq.question: Can AI send or delete messages automatically?
faq.answer: No. AI is limited to selected-context assistance and drafts that require user review; it cannot send, delete or silently change recipients.

faq.question: How is Mail recovery handled?
faq.answer: A local operator backup and restore drill preserves authenticated state, provider recovery records and sender identity inside a restricted encrypted backup boundary. Prior-binary rollback remains unverified.
